content.comment_body: Hello all, how can I connect to [product_name] from an external network over the internet? Access works on my local network. I followed the example from [user_name] but couldn't get it working for myself. The router's external IP address is dynamic, not fixed. Any guidance is appreciated.

Hi, if your router does not use a static IP address, you need a Dynamic DNS service to reach [product_name] without using the IP directly. With Dyn-DNS, you can assign a recognizable name like 'my_device_at_home' to your device. You can search for Dyn-DNS providers using Google. Make sure to set up port forwarding in your router, and a VPN connection may be needed. Also, enable remote access in your [product_name] settings. Hope this is helpful.

Thanks for your response. Is there an alternative to DynDNS? I'm looking for a free solution. Currently, I can connect to [product_name] through the web server in my LAN. The router IP is 192.168.1.1, PC uses a dynamic IP, and [product_name] has IP 192.168.0.3, with subnet mask 255.255.255.0, and gateway set to 0.0.0.0. [product_name] software is configured for IP 192.168.0.3 with the same mask and gateway. I checked my public IP at [url] and it changes frequently. What should I do? Any help is welcome.

It's challenging for those trying to help when details are unclear. Please specify what exactly you're aiming to do (for example, web server access) so we can assist you properly. From where and using which method do you want to reach the web server?
The IP address shown by 'WhatIsMyIp' is the one your internet provider assigns for external access. To find your PC's IP, use the 'ipconfig' command in a Windows command prompt.
My goal is to access the web server from the internet.

Do you have a static IP provided by your internet service, or not? If yes, you can use [product_name]'s IP for direct remote access. If not, you can only connect as long as the router IP doesn't change. The main solution I know is to use a Dynamic DNS service. Some Dyn-DNS services are available for free or with limited options—searching for them in Google might help. Hope this clarifies things.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are struggling to access [product_name]'s web server remotely due to changing external IPs from their providers. The absence of a static IP complicates direct connectivity. Most advice centers around Dynamic DNS services and router port forwarding, but users prefer simple, free alternatives and clearer step-by-step instructions for setting up remote access.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want convenient and reliable access to [product_name]'s web server from the internet, ideally using free services and straightforward configuration steps without depending on paid Dynamic DNS providers or complex networking requirements.
